Title: ASCII Art-based Jailbreak Attacks against Aligned LLMs

In this paper, the authors propose a novel jailbreak attack, called ArtPrompt, which exploits the limitations of large language models (LLMs) in recognizing ASCII art to bypass safety measures and elicit undesired behaviors. The authors develop a benchmark, Vision-in-Text Challenge (VITC), to evaluate the capabilities of five state-of-the-art LLMs (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Gemini, Claude, and Llama2) in recognizing prompts that cannot be solely interpreted by semantics. The results show that all five LLMs struggle to understand input queries that use ASCII art to represent one single letter or number, and the ability of the LLMs to correctly recognize input queries drops significantly as the input queries contain more letters or numbers. The authors then use the limitations of LLMs in recognizing ASCII art to launch the ArtPrompt attack, which consists of two steps: finding words within a given prompt that may trigger rejections from LLM, and crafting a set of cloaked prompts by visually encoding the identified words using ASCII art. The authors evaluate the effectiveness and efficiency of ArtPrompt on five SOTA LLMs and show that it can effectively and efficiently induce undesired behaviors from all five LLMs.

Summary of Attack Methods:

This paper proposes a novel jailbreak attack, called ArtPrompt, which exploits the limitations of large language models (LLMs) in recognizing ASCII art to bypass safety measures and elicit undesired behaviors from LLMs. The attack consists of two steps: (1) finding words within a prompt that may trigger rejections from LLM, and (2) crafting a set of cloaked prompts by visually encoding the identified words using ASCII art. The authors evaluate ArtPrompt on five state-of-the-art LLMs and show that it can effectively and efficiently induce undesired behaviors from all five models. The paper also introduces a benchmark, Vision-in-Text Challenge (VITC), to evaluate the capabilities of LLMs in recognizing prompts that cannot be solely interpreted by semantics. The key contributions of the paper are:

* The proposal of ArtPrompt, a novel jailbreak attack that exploits the limitations of LLMs in recognizing ASCII art.
* The introduction of VITC, a benchmark to evaluate the capabilities of LLMs in recognizing prompts that cannot be solely interpreted by semantics.
* The demonstration of the effectiveness and efficiency of ArtPrompt in inducing undesired behaviors from five state-of-the-art LLMs.

Introduction to the Mechanism of Success

In this section, the authors introduce the mechanism of success for their proposed jailbreak attack, ArtPrompt. They explain that the attack exploits the limitations of large language models (LLMs) in recognizing ASCII art, which can be used to bypass safety measures and elicit undesired behaviors from the models. The authors highlight the significance of their findings, as existing techniques for ensuring LLM safety only consider the semantic interpretation of natural language and neglect the possibility of interpretation based on the arrangement of characters within the input space. They also introduce the Vision-in-Text Challenge (VITC) benchmark, which they use to evaluate the capabilities of five state-of-the-art LLMs in recognizing prompts that contain ASCII art. The authors' contributions include the development of ArtPrompt, a novel jailbreak attack that leverages the poor performance of LLMs in recognizing ASCII art, and the introduction of VITC as a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating LLM capabilities in this area.

Related Work:

Several techniques have been proposed to enhance the safety of large language models (LLMs), including data filtering and supervised fine-tuning (Bakker et al., 2022; Wei et al., 2023a). However, these approaches focus solely on the semantic interpretation of natural language, overlooking the fact that corpora can be interpreted in multiple ways beyond semantics. In this paper, we propose a novel benchmark, the Vision-in-Text Challenge (VITC), to evaluate the capabilities of LLMs in recognizing prompts that cannot be solely interpreted by semantics. Our results indicate that five state-of-the-art LLMs (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Gemini, Claude, and Llama2) struggle to recognize prompts provided in the form of ASCII art. This vulnerability can be exploited by a novel jailbreak attack, ArtPrompt, which leverages the poor performance of LLMs in recognizing ASCII art to bypass safety measures and elicit undesired behaviors from LLMs.

The key contributions of this paper are:

1. The development of VITC, a benchmark to evaluate the capabilities of LLMs in recognizing prompts that cannot be solely interpreted by semantics.
2. The discovery of vulnerabilities in five state-of-the-art LLMs in recognizing ASCII art, which can be exploited by the proposed jailbreak attack, ArtPrompt.
3. The introduction of ArtPrompt, a novel jailbreak attack that leverages the poor performance of LLMs in recognizing ASCII art to bypass safety measures and elicit undesired behaviors from LLMs.

The main difference between this paper and previous work is the focus on the limitations of LLMs in recognizing prompts that cannot be solely interpreted by semantics, and the exploitation of these limitations to develop a novel jailbreak attack. Previous work has primarily focused on improving the safety of LLMs through data filtering and supervised fine-tuning, without considering the potential vulnerabilities that can arise from the interpretation of corpora in multiple ways beyond semantics.
